title: Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint — Internal Brief (Sales/CS Enablement Deck Outline)
author: Avery Johnson
body:
## Purpose (read this first)
This page is the **internal brief deck outline** for the Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint. It is designed to align **Sales + Customer Success/Support** on what’s changing in the self-serve onboarding experience, why we’re changing it, and how to handle inbound questions.

**What you should take away:**
- What will look different to prospects/users (emails, console nudges, retargeting).
- What we are (and are not) promising in messaging.
- What Sales/CS should watch for during the sprint (confusion signals, escalation triggers).
- Where to route issues fast (ops, product, engineering, support).

---

## Deck metadata
- **Deck name:** Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint — Internal Brief
- **Audience:** Sales, CS, Support, Solutions Engineering, Partnerships
- **Presenter (default):** Ben Carter (Growth) + Avery Johnson (Sales) + Aparna Reddy (CS)
- **Duration:** 15 minutes + 10 minutes Q&A
- **When to present:** Week 0 kickoff; quick refresh in Week 1 within team meetings

---

## Slide-by-slide outline

### Slide 1 — Title / Why you’re seeing this
**Title:** Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint: What’s changing + how to handle customer questions
**Speaker notes:** We are running a 3-week sprint to improve self-serve activation + early retention. Sales/CS will likely see more inbound questions; we want tight feedback loops and clean escalation.

### Slide 2 — Executive summary (one slide)
**What’s changing (3 levers):**
1) Onboarding email sequences (welcome → first success → troubleshooting → next step)
2) In-console nudges (setup checklist + contextual banners)
3) Retargeting for non-activated and recently lapsed users

**Why it matters:** Faster time-to-first-success, fewer avoidable support tickets, clearer “next step” motions into higher intent.

**What Sales/CS should do:** Flag confusion early, track recurring blockers, avoid over-promising, route issues via the defined escalation paths.

### Slide 3 — Goals + definitions (so we’re aligned)
**Primary goal:** Lift activation and early retention for self-serve developers.

**Activation (sprint definition):** A user reaches “first successful production-like inference call.”
- Operationally measured via product events (see “Metrics & instrumentation” slide)

**Secondary milestones we want to increase:**
- Billing added
- Token usage ramps beyond “testing”
- Deployment/route created
- Teammate invited

### Slide 4 — Who is affected (segments)
**Included:**
- New self-serve signups (API-first developers)
- Non-activated signups (no first success within 24h/72h)
- Recently lapsed users (no activity in a defined window)

**Not targeted in this sprint (by design):**
- Enterprise accounts under active Sales cycles where lifecycle automation could conflict with bespoke onboarding
- Regulated prospects where messaging must stay conservative (VPC/on-prem conversations stay sales-assisted)

**Speaker notes:** If you see a strategic account getting lifecycle touches unexpectedly, treat as an escalation (see later slide).

### Slide 5 — What’s changing: onboarding emails
**What users will experience:**
- A 5-email series over the first ~7–10 days, with suppression rules based on activation progress.

**High-level email intents:**
1) Welcome + quickstart CTA
2) First request success (copy/paste snippet + key creation)
3) Streaming + latency basics
4) Troubleshooting: common errors + how to get help
5) Next step: cost dashboard + routes/deployments + invite teammate

**What’s new vs. old:**
- More explicit “first success” path and fewer generic marketing messages.
- Troubleshooting is earlier and more contextual.

**Sales/CS callout:** Be prepared for “Why am I getting this?” and “How do I stop?” questions (see FAQ slide).

### Slide 6 — What’s changing: in-console nudges (checklist + banners)
**Nudges included in v1:**
- A setup checklist (key creation, first request, enable streaming, view latency/cost dashboard)
- Two contextual banners (e.g., missing key, repeated request errors)

**Trigger logic (simplified):**
- Nudges appear when a user is missing an activation step, and hide after success events are seen.
- Nudges are behind a feature flag and rolled out via experiment assignments.

**Speaker notes:** Expect screenshots in tickets. Ask users to paste banner copy; small copy differences may indicate experiment variants.

### Slide 7 — What’s changing: retargeting (LinkedIn/Google)
**Audience:**
- Non-activated signups
- Recently lapsed users

**Messaging constraints:**
- Developer-first tone; focus on latency/cost/reliability, and clear “first success” CTA.
- Benchmarks and claims must link to substantiation.

**Landing page expectation:**
- Quickstart first, benchmarks second, troubleshooting prominent

**Sales/CS callout:** Prospects may reference ad claims; do not improvise numbers. Use approved proof points and links.

### Slide 8 — Timeline / rollout plan
**Week 0 (Setup):** tracking, copy approvals, UX specs, audience rules, suppression lists, feature flags
**Week 1 (Launch v1):** email v1 + console nudge v1 + retargeting audiences live
**Week 2 (Iterate):** A/B variants, copy tweaks, bug fixes; tighten suppressions if needed
**Week 3 (Readout):** results + decision (roll-forward / rollback / new hypotheses)

**Rollbacks:**
- Emails: pause sends + widen suppressions
- Console: flip feature flag off; revert banner placements
- Retargeting: pause campaigns; refresh exclusions

### Slide 9 — Metrics, instrumentation, and what you’ll hear in readouts
**Primary metrics:**
- Activation rate within 24h / 72h
- Time-to-first-success
- D7 / D14 retention

**Guardrails:**
- Unsubscribes and spam complaints
- Support ticket volume and category spikes
- Console performance/SLO checks

**How Sales/CS can help:**
- Tag inbound issues as “Activation blocker” with the closest category (auth, streaming, model selection, console UX, docs)
- Share qualitative snippets (what they tried, what they expected, exact error/banner text)

### Slide 10 — What Sales should watch for (signals + actions)
**Signals we care about (good):**
- “I got to first request quickly”
- “The streaming example worked”
- “Cost dashboard clarified spend”

**Signals we care about (bad / sales-assist triggers):**
- Repeated confusion about deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Security/compliance questions appearing earlier due to lifecycle messaging
- Any sense that we are “spamming” or mis-targeting contacts

**Recommended Sales actions:**
- If a prospect is mid-cycle: confirm they’re not being confused by automated onboarding touches.
- Use the approved talk track: Redwood is optimizing the default path to first success; enterprise paths remain supported.

### Slide 11 — What CS/Support should watch for (common failure modes)
**Likely issues during sprint:**
- API key creation/permissions confusion
- First request 4xx/5xx errors; unclear error messages
- Streaming disconnects (client-side) attributed to platform
- Email links leading to the wrong console path (routing changes)
- Opt-out/suppression not honored (compliance-sensitive)

**CS/Support actions:**
- Capture: user/org ID, SDK used, region, timestamps, exact error payload if possible
- Route per escalation slide; do not “patch” copy or promises in the moment

### Slide 12 — Escalation paths (fast routing)
Use this decision tree when lifecycle changes cause confusion or risk:

**A) Compliance / opt-out / “stop emailing me” / suppression bug**
- Owner: Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)
- Backup: Camila Reyes (Exec sponsor)
- Action: Treat as urgent; stop sends if needed; document the contact + timestamp

**B) Console nudge confusion or UX regression**
- Owner: Marissa Cole (Product, Console)
- Eng: Chloe Martin (Console Eng) / Jada Williams (Experimentation)
- Action: Provide screenshot + URL + banner copy + time + user/org ID

**C) Event tracking / attribution weirdness**
- Owner: Paula Mendes (Telemetry requirements) / Logan Wright (Analytics platform)
- Action: Include event name, expected properties, sample request IDs

**D) Performance/SLO concerns**
- Owner: Sean Gallagher (SLO/guardrails)
- Action: Flag immediately with time window, suspected correlation (e.g., checklist load)

**Channels to use:**
- #marketing (emails, retargeting, suppression)
- #product (activation definition, UX scope)
- #support (ticket spikes, user confusion)
- #eng-platform (event schema, analytics payload validation)

### Slide 13 — Approved talk track (what to say / what not to say)
**What to say (approved themes):**
- “We’re making it faster to get to a first successful inference call with clearer quickstarts and in-console guidance.”
- “If you’re evaluating for production, we can support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments—let’s align on your constraints.”
- “If anything in onboarding feels off, we want the feedback. We’re iterating quickly this month.”

**What NOT to say:**
- Do not quote benchmark numbers unless you can link the source.
- Do not claim an SLA for Hosted unless the contract explicitly includes it.
- Do not promise that a specific experiment variant will remain (these are tests).

### Slide 14 — FAQ (for inbound)
**Q: Why am I getting these onboarding emails?**
A: You signed up for Redwood and these emails are intended to help you reach first success quickly. If you’d like, we can pause them or you can unsubscribe.

**Q: I unsubscribed but still got an email.**
A: Apologize, confirm the address, and escalate immediately to Marketing Ops (compliance-sensitive). Do not ask them to “wait for it to update.”

**Q: The console banner says to do X, but I already did it.**
A: Ask when they completed the step and what SDK/region they used; it may be an event tracking delay or variant mismatch. Escalate with screenshot + timestamps.

**Q: Are you saying Hosted is always cheaper/faster than self-hosting?**
A: No—cost and performance depend on workload. We provide tooling and options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) to meet latency/cost/reliability requirements.

### Slide 15 — How to provide feedback (so it’s actionable)
When escalating, include:
- What user was trying to do (key creation, first request, streaming)
- SDK or curl, region, and approximate time
- Exact error text and/or request ID
- Screenshot of banner/email (including the CTA link)
- Whether this is a one-off or repeated across multiple accounts

---

## Appendix (optional slides / backup)
### Backup slide A — Event names (high-level)
For reference in debugging and readouts (not exhaustive):
- api_key_created
- first_request_success (first 2xx completion)
- first_streaming_success
- dashboard_viewed (latency/cost)
- billing_added
- route_created
- teammate_invited

### Backup slide B — Guardrail thresholds (operational)
- Unsubscribe spike: investigate within same business day; consider throttling/pausing
- Support spike: if activation-related tickets materially increase week-over-week, convene triage (Support + Product + Growth)
- Console performance: any measurable degradation correlated to the checklist feature flag requires rollback consideration
